records.summary: Tasaki Problem 2.1.g / eq. (2.1.34), p. 20: the general-spin closed form of the pi-rotation about axis 1, spinSPiRotation1 N, equals the exponential exp(-i*pi*S^{(1)}) via spinSRot1 N Real.pi. Identified by the commutant argument: the pi-conjugations of the axis-1 rotation and of the spin-reversal operator agree on the generators Ŝ^{1,2,3}, hence their ratio is central (Problem 2.1.a, p. 15, spanning) and therefore scalar; the scalar is pinned to 1 by evaluating both sides on the explicit binomial top vector spinSTopVector. The identification of all three single-site closed forms with exp(-i*pi*S^{(alpha)}) at general S is proved (spinSPiRotation3_eq_spinSRot3_pi, spinSPiRotation1_eq_spinSRot1_pi, spinSPiRotation2_eq_exp_spinSOp2), so the coverage of the source item is complete.

Tasaki Problem 2.1.g / eq. (2.1.34), p. 20: the general-spin closed form of the pi-rotation about axis 2, spinSPiRotation2 N, equals the exponential exp(-i*pi*S^{(2)}) via spinSRot3 N (pi/2) * spinSRot1 N pi * spinSRot3 N (-(pi/2)). Identified by conjugating the axis-1 exponential by the quarter turn about axis 3 (spinSRot3_pi_half_conj_spinSPiRotation1, exp_neg_pi_mul_I_spinSOp2_eq_spinSRot3_conj); the printed cyclic relation (2.1.29), p. 19, then follows as a theorem about exponentials rather than a definitional assumption, and the printed entry form (-1)^{S+sigma} delta_{sigma,-tau} of the second relation of (2.1.34) is stated at general S in the integer basis index (spinSPiRotation2_apply). The identification of all three single-site closed forms with exp(-i*pi*S^{(alpha)}) at general S is proved (spinSPiRotation3_eq_spinSRot3_pi, spinSPiRotation1_eq_spinSRot1_pi, spinSPiRotation2_eq_exp_spinSOp2), so the coverage of the source item is complete.

Tasaki Problem 2.2.a (b): for alpha and beta distinct, the global pi-rotations U_pi^{(alpha)} and U_pi^{(beta)} anticommute whenever |Lambda|*N is odd, i.e. |Lambda|*S is a half-odd integer. Proved for the closed-form pi-rotation matrices spinSPiRotationAxis and their uniform lattice tensor manyBodySPiRotation; the identification of all three single-site closed forms with exp(-i*pi*S^{(alpha)}) at general S is proved (spinSPiRotation3_eq_spinSRot3_pi, spinSPiRotation1_eq_spinSRot1_pi, spinSPiRotation2_eq_exp_spinSOp2), and the many-body lift is also proved (manyBodySPiRotation_eq_exp), so the statement is restated on the book's exponential objects as manyBodySPiRotationExp_anticommute_of_odd; the coverage of the source item is complete.

Tasaki Problem 2.2.a (a): for alpha and beta distinct, the global pi-rotations U_pi^{(alpha)} and U_pi^{(beta)} commute whenever |Lambda|*N is even, i.e. |Lambda|*S is an integer. Proved for the closed-form pi-rotation matrices spinSPiRotationAxis and their uniform lattice tensor manyBodySPiRotation; the identification of all three single-site closed forms with exp(-i*pi*S^{(alpha)}) at general S is proved (spinSPiRotation3_eq_spinSRot3_pi, spinSPiRotation1_eq_spinSRot1_pi, spinSPiRotation2_eq_exp_spinSOp2), and the many-body lift is also proved (manyBodySPiRotation_eq_exp), so the statement is restated on the book's exponential objects as manyBodySPiRotationExp_commute_of_even; the coverage of the source item is complete.

Tasaki Problem 2.2.a (c): when |Lambda|*N is odd, every nonzero eigenvector of the global pi-rotation U_pi^{(alpha)} is orthogonal to its image under the anticommuting global pi-rotation U_pi^{(beta)}, alpha and beta distinct. Proved for the closed-form pi-rotation matrices spinSPiRotationAxis and their uniform lattice tensor manyBodySPiRotation; the identification of all three single-site closed forms with exp(-i*pi*S^{(alpha)}) at general S is proved (spinSPiRotation3_eq_spinSRot3_pi, spinSPiRotation1_eq_spinSRot1_pi, spinSPiRotation2_eq_exp_spinSOp2), and the many-body lift is also proved (manyBodySPiRotation_eq_exp), so the statement is restated on the book's exponential objects as tasaki_problem_2_2_a_exp_eigenvector_orthogonal, the terminal theorem of the Problem 2.2.a chain named by the legacy catalogue; the coverage of the source item is complete.

Tasaki eq. (2.2.11), p. 22, at theta = pi, the definition of the global pi rotations of Problem 2.2.a, p. 23: the global pi rotation manyBodySPiRotation Lambda N alpha, the uniform lattice tensor of the single-site closed form, equals exp(-i*pi*S_tot^{(alpha)}) for every axis alpha in Fin 3, so the closed-form global rotations on which the Problem 2.2.a statements are proved are the exponentials the book writes. The site embedding onSiteS is shown to be a continuous ring homomorphism, hence commutes with the matrix exponential (onSiteS_exp); a many-body tensor is the Finset.noncommProd of the site embeddings of its factors (manyBodyTensorS_eq_noncommProd); since distinct-site embeddings commute, the exponential of their sum is that product (manyBodyTensorS_const_exp). Combined with the single-site closed forms of eq. (2.1.34), p. 20 (spinSPiRotationAxis_eq_exp), this gives the identity.

Tasaki Problem 2.2.b, eq. (2.2.14), p. 23, the first display: the SU(2)-averaged two-site state (1/4*pi) * integral over phi in [0,2*pi], theta in [0,pi] of sin(theta) * (U^(3)_phi U^(2)_theta) applied to |up_1 down_2> equals (1/2)(|up_1 down_2> - |down_1 up_2>), stated component-wise at every configuration tau, where U^(alpha)_theta = exp(-i*theta*S_tot^(alpha)) as in eq. (2.2.11), p. 22; the second conjunct identifies this result with (1/sqrt(2))|Phi_{0,0}>, the two-site singlet twoSiteSinglet of Appendix A.3.3, eq. (A.3.23), p. 474. The coverage of the source item is complete for this display.

The Pauli X matrix squares to the identity.

On a connected graph with a real, symmetric, edge-supported, strictly ferromagnetic spin-S coupling, the eigenspace of the Heisenberg Hamiltonian alone at the saturated-ferromagnet energy equals the linear span of the ladder family generated from the all-up state; this is the H-only ground-state eigenspace identity of Tasaki's Theorem 2.1, for a weighted generalisation of the printed uniform coupling.

On a connected graph with a real, symmetric, edge-supported, strictly ferromagnetic spin-S coupling at the printed uniform strength, the Heisenberg Hamiltonian minus its ground energy is positive semidefinite, its ground eigenspace equals the linear span of the ladder family generated from the all-up state, i.e. the states of eq. (2.4.10), and that eigenspace has dimension |V|*N + 1 = 2*S_max + 1. The companion joint-eigenspace result in the same module adds that every ground state has maximal total spin; the printed converse, that these are the only states of maximal total spin, is not proved.

On a connected graph with a real, symmetric, edge-supported, strictly ferromagnetic spin-S coupling, the eigenspace of the Heisenberg Hamiltonian alone at the saturated-ferromagnet energy equals the joint eigenspace of that Hamiltonian and the total-spin Casimir at the saturated values; this is the ground-state half of Tasaki's remark after eq. (2.4.10), that every ferromagnetic ground state carries maximal total spin, and not the converse inclusion the remark also asserts.
